steps.description: We will look at the `Yearn V2 vault interface` that `Alchemix` calls when it deposits yield-bearing collateral, follows gains, and respects `Yearn’s governance`. By the end you will know the meaning of every public field and method used in the integration.

The vault tracks every attached strategy with the `StrategyParams` **struct**:
- line 10  `performanceFee` – % of profits the strategy keeps.
- line 11  `activation` – first time the strategy was added.
- line 12  `debtRatio` – share of vault assets it may borrow.
- lines 13-14  `minDebtPerHarvest`/`maxDebtPerHarvest` – size bounds each harvest may raise debt by.
- line 15  `lastReport` – last block the strategy called `report()`.
- line 16  `totalDebt` – principal borrowed from the vault.
- lines 17-18  `totalGain` / `totalLoss` – cumulative pnl.
- line 19  `enforceChangeLimit` – whether the next two ratios are enforced.
- lines 20-21  `profitLimitRatio` / `lossLimitRatio` – relative harvest change caps.
- line 22  `customCheck` – optional contract hook used by governance.

Depositing yields `Yearn` shares. `Vyper` creates three overloads so that callers may omit optional arguments:
- `deposit()` – move full `ERC-20` balance to the vault and send shares back to `msg.sender`.
- `deposit(amount)` – specify token amount, still receive shares yourself.
- `deposit(amount, recipient)` – specify both amount and the address that receives the `yvTokens`.
`Alchemix` typically uses the second form when it pushes a precise collateral quantity.

Withdraw is symmetrical, again with defaulted arguments:
- `withdraw()` – burn all caller shares and redeem underlying to caller.
- `withdraw(maxShares)` – burn at most that many shares.
- `withdraw(maxShares, recipient)` – send the underlying elsewhere.
- `withdraw(maxShares, recipient, maxLoss)` – tolerate slippage up to maxLoss (basis-points).
`Alchemix` uses these when users unwrap yvTokens back to the base asset.

Size & limit helpers frequently polled by front-ends:
- `token()` → **ERC-20** deposited.
- `strategies(addr)` → fetch the `StrategyParams` shown earlier.
- `pricePerShare()` – current value of one `yvToken` in base units; **Alchemix** multiplies this by share balance to value collateral.
- `totalAssets()` – aggregate base tokens managed by vault.
- `depositLimit()` – hard cap that governance can impose.
- `maxAvailableShares()` – shares that could be withdrawn right now without touching strategies.

On-chain accounting used by strategies:
- `creditAvailable()` – how much more this strategy may borrow this block.
- `debtOutstanding()` – amount the vault wants repaid now.
- `expectedReturn()` – profit the strategy should be able to realise.
Although Alchemix is not itself a strategy contract, these three views drive Yearn’s internal rebalancing and thus indirectly affect the pricePerShare that Alchemix observes.

`report(gain, loss, debtPayment)` is the single state-mutating hook every strategy must call after harvesting. It updates the `StrategyParams` shown on slide 2 and redistributes fees. Down-stream effects ultimately surface in `pricePerShare()`.

Governance endpoints a protocol integrator may want to read:
- `apiVersion()` – semantic version of the vault code, helpful for migrations.
- `governance()` – address allowed to enact owner-level changes.
- `management()` – ops address with reduced permissions.
- `guardian()` – emergency address that can trigger shutdowns.
`Alchemix` monitors these so that it can react if a vault it is using changes control.

You have now walked the entire `Yearn V2 public API`: data that measures strategy performance, overloaded `deposit/withdraw` entry points, real-time accounting helpers, the mandatory `report` call, and governance accessors. These pieces form the lifecycle from depositing `Alchemix collateral`, through yield generation, to eventual withdrawal while staying aware of `vault limits` and control addresses.
